title: Exploring and Mitigating Failure Behavior of Large Language Model Training Workloads in HPC Systems
problem: LLM training on HPC systems faces reliability challenges from transient faults; failure patterns are more complex than DNN inference due to massive parameter scale and iterative updates
motivation: Exponential growth in LLM training demand; transient faults increasingly common; understanding failure modes and enabling recovery is critical for large-scale training
method: They created LLMFI, a tool that injects simulated hardware faults into LLM training to observe resulting failures. Running over 300,000 of these experiments across 5,000+ GPU hours revealed distinct failure patterns. They then developed LLMFT, an ML-based framework that continuously monitors for these failures (using extracted system features and a fault detector) and automatically applies recovery strategies to resume training.
key_novelty: They identified six distinct failure modes in LLM training on HPC systems and built an ML-based closed-loop control system (continuous monitoring with automatic targeted recovery) to handle each one.
contributions: LLMFI fault injection tool for LLM training
97.61% F1-score fault detection with minimal overhead
baselines: Existing resilience approaches for DNN inference
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific LLM training setups; generalization to other models/scales uncertain
primary_theme: Fault tolerance and resilience for LLM training at scale
